messages.subject: strange behaviour generate.mirt.object()
parts:
hi phil,

i had an error in my code, but correcting it makes things strange :P i use mirt.generate.object() to specify an IRT model and then pass a df to fscores to compute theta scores. however, i had -1 values in the response df, which were incorrectly coded. i got valid theta estimates nonetheless. the strange thing is then that when i correct those and set them to NA i get different theta estimates for other (unchanged) response patterns as well. see minimal example attached.

would be glad if you could check, whats happening here, 
best, felix

    d4 = c(7.03515209077744, 7.69398240013824, 5.18848696304847, 
        6.27769024323888, NA, NA, NA)), .Names = c("item_mod", "a1", 
            "d0", "d1", "d2", "d3", "d4"), row.names = c(NA, -7L), class = "data.frame")
model = generate.mirt_object(pars[,-1], itemtype = "gpcm")
resp = structure(list(freun02 = c(3, 4, 4, 2, 2, 4, 1, 4, 2, 3), freun03 = c(3, 
    4, 4, 2, 3, 4, 1, 4, 3, 2), freun06 = c(2, 4, 4, 1, 2, 4, 0, 
        4, 2, 3), freun07 = c(3, 4, 4, 2, 2, 4, 0, 4, 1, 4), freun20 = c(2, 
            2, 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, NA, NA), freun24r = c(2, 2, 2, 0, 1, 1, 
                NA, 3, -1, 3), freun25r = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, -1, 
                    1)), .Names = c("freun02", "freun03", "freun06", "freun07", "freun20", 
                        "freun24r", "freun25r"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(1L, 
                            3L, 6L, 7L, 11L, 12L, 14L, 18L, 19L, 24L))

fscores(model, response.pattern = resp)
resp[resp == -1] = NA
fscores(model, response.pattern = resp)

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: strange behaviour generate.mirt.object()
parts:
The -1's are the problem here. In the generate.mirt_object documentation I put this: 

"min_category: the value representing the lowest category index. By default this is 0, therefore the respond suitable for the first category is 0, second is 1, and so on up to K - 1"

So a value of -1 is outside the expected range, and really is just confusing the internal functions because they doesn't know what to do with these values. So either make all the lowest categories equal to 0, or modify the min_category input to change the 0 default. HTH.

Phil
